blocks.content:
According to Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of:
• President of India
• Lok Sabha (House of the People)
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States)
Important Note:
The President is an integral part of Parliament but is not a member of either House.

items: Article 79 Question: Remember that the President IS part of the Parliament. A common trap in MCQs is excluding the President from Parliament's definition.
Membership Trap: Although the President is an integral part of Parliament, he/she is NOT a member of either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.
Terminologies: Be clear with the English and Hindi nomenclature — Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 79 lays down the constitutional structure and composition of the Indian Parliament.
The Parliament of India comprises three distinct components: the President of India, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha.
Lok Sabha is formally known as the House of the People.
Rajya Sabha is formally known as the Council of States.
The President holds a unique position as an integral part of Parliament without holding membership in either House.
